name: Geology
description: The study of the solid Earth, its rocks, structure, processes, and history.

name: Geophysics
description: The study of the Earth through its physical properties and fields, including seismic, magnetic, and gravity.

name: Geochemistry
description: The study of the chemical composition of the Earth and the chemical processes within it.

name: Petrology
description: The study of the origin, composition, and structure of rocks.

name: Mineralogy
description: The study of minerals, their chemistry, crystal structure, and properties.

name: Paleontology
description: The study of ancient life through fossils.

name: Sedimentology
description: The study of sediments and sedimentary processes and rocks.

name: Stratigraphy
description: The study of rock layers and their chronological relationships.

name: Structural Geology
description: The study of rock deformation, faults, folds, and tectonic structures.

name: Geomorphology
description: The study of landforms and the processes that shape the Earth's surface.

name: Hydrology
description: The study of the distribution, movement, and quality of water on Earth.

name: Volcanology
description: The study of volcanoes, magma, and volcanic phenomena.

name: Soil Science
description: The study of soil as a natural resource, its formation, classification, and use.

name: Glaciology
description: The study of glaciers, ice sheets, and their dynamics.

name: Planetary Geology
description: The application of geological methods to the study of other planets and moons.

name: Economic Geology
description: The study of geological materials of economic value, including ores and fuels.

name: Geobiology
description: The study of interactions between life and the Earth's physical environment over time.

name: Limnology
description: The study of inland freshwater bodies such as lakes, rivers, and wetlands.

name: Historical Geology
description: The reconstruction of Earth's history from the rock record.

name: Regional Geology
description: The geological character and history of specific regions.

name: Field Geology
description: The direct observation and mapping of rocks and structures in the field.

name: Environmental Geology
description: The application of geology to environmental problems and hazards.

name: Engineering Geology
description: The application of geology to engineering design and construction safety.

name: Marine Geology
description: The geology of the ocean floor and continental margins.

name: Quaternary Geology
description: The study of the most recent geological period, including ice ages and recent landforms.

name: Seismology
description: The study of earthquakes and the propagation of seismic waves through the Earth.

name: Earthquake Seismology
description: The study of earthquake sources, mechanisms, and ground motion.

name: Seismic Tomography
description: Imaging of Earth's interior using seismic wave travel times.

name: Paleoseismology
description: The study of prehistoric earthquakes from geological evidence.

name: Strong Motion Seismology
description: The study of strong ground shaking and its effects on structures.

name: Engineering Seismology
description: The application of seismology to earthquake-resistant design.

name: Geomagnetism
description: The study of Earth's magnetic field and its origin and variation.

name: Gravimetry
description: The measurement and study of Earth's gravity field.

name: Geodesy
description: The measurement and representation of Earth's shape, orientation, and gravity field.

name: Satellite Geodesy
description: Geodetic measurement using satellite positioning and altimetry systems.

name: Geothermics
description: The study of Earth's internal heat and geothermal energy.

name: Geodynamics
description: The study of the forces and motions driving Earth's interior and plates.

name: Exploration Geophysics
description: The use of geophysical methods to locate subsurface resources.

name: Rock Physics
description: The study of the physical properties of rocks under various conditions.

name: Isotope Geochemistry
description: The use of isotope ratios to trace geological processes and dates.

name: Stable Isotope Geochemistry
description: The use of stable isotope ratios as tracers of environmental and geological processes.

name: Geochronology
description: The science of dating rocks, minerals, and fossils.

name: Radiometric Dating
description: Determination of absolute ages using radioactive decay of isotopes.

name: Organic Geochemistry
description: The study of organic matter in sediments and the formation of fossil fuels.

name: Aqueous Geochemistry
description: The chemistry of natural waters interacting with rocks and minerals.

name: Trace Element Geochemistry
description: The distribution and behavior of trace elements in geological systems.

name: Biogeochemistry
description: The chemical, physical, and biological processes governing element cycles in the environment.

name: Cosmochemistry
description: The chemistry of extraterrestrial materials such as meteorites.

name: Petroleum Geochemistry
description: The chemical study of petroleum formation, migration, and composition.

name: Igneous Petrology
description: The study of rocks formed from cooling magma or lava.

name: Sedimentary Petrology
description: The study of rocks formed from deposited and lithified sediment.

name: Metamorphic Petrology
description: The study of rocks transformed by heat, pressure, and fluids.

name: Experimental Petrology
description: Laboratory simulation of the conditions of rock formation.

name: Crystallography
description: The study of crystal structure, symmetry, and lattice arrangement.

name: Crystal Chemistry
description: The relationship between crystal structure and chemical composition.

name: Optical Mineralogy
description: The identification of minerals by their optical properties under polarized light.

name: Descriptive Mineralogy
description: The systematic description and classification of mineral species.

name: Gemology
description: The study of gemstones and their identification and valuation.

name: Clay Mineralogy
description: The study of clay minerals and their structure and properties.

name: Biomineralogy
description: The study of minerals formed by biological processes.

name: Invertebrate Paleontology
description: The study of fossil invertebrates.

name: Vertebrate Paleontology
description: The study of fossil vertebrates including dinosaurs and early mammals.

name: Micropaleontology
description: The study of microscopic fossils such as foraminifera and diatoms.

name: Paleobotany
description: The study of fossil plants.

name: Palynology
description: The study of pollen, spores, and other organic microfossils.

name: Paleoecology
description: The reconstruction of ancient ecosystems from fossil evidence.

name: Paleoclimatology
description: The study of past climates from geological and fossil records.

name: Ichnology
description: The study of trace fossils such as tracks, burrows, and trails.

name: Taphonomy
description: The study of the processes of fossilization and preservation.

name: Biostratigraphy
description: The use of fossils to date and correlate rock layers.

name: Clastic Sedimentology
description: The study of sediments derived from weathered rock fragments.

name: Carbonate Sedimentology
description: The study of carbonate sediments and rocks such as limestone.

name: Diagenesis
description: The physical and chemical changes converting sediment into rock.

name: Sequence Stratigraphy
description: The study of sedimentary packages bounded by unconformities in relation to sea-level change.

name: Basin Analysis
description: The integrated study of sedimentary basins and their evolution.

name: Lithostratigraphy
description: The subdivision of rock sequences based on lithology.

name: Chronostratigraphy
description: The dating and subdivision of strata by geological time.

name: Magnetostratigraphy
description: The correlation of strata using magnetic polarity reversals.

name: Chemostratigraphy
description: The correlation of strata using chemical signatures.

name: Tectonics
description: The study of the large-scale structure and deformation of Earth's crust.

name: Plate Tectonics
description: The theory of the motion and interaction of Earth's lithospheric plates.

name: Neotectonics
description: The study of recent and ongoing crustal deformation.

name: Rock Deformation
description: The study of how rocks strain and deform under stress.

name: Microtectonics
description: The study of deformation at microscopic and grain scale.

name: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: The study of rivers and the landforms they create.

name: Glacial Geomorphology
description: The study of landforms created by glaciers and ice sheets.

name: Coastal Geomorphology
description: The study of coastal landforms and shoreline processes.

name: Aeolian Geomorphology
description: The study of wind-formed landforms such as dunes.

name: Karst Geomorphology
description: The study of dissolution landforms in soluble rock.

name: Tectonic Geomorphology
description: The study of how tectonics shapes landforms and landscapes.

name: Surface Hydrology
description: The study of surface water flow, runoff, and streams.

name: Hydrogeology
description: The study of groundwater occurrence, flow, and aquifers.

name: Catchment Hydrology
description: The study of water movement within drainage basins.

name: Hydrometry
description: The measurement of water flow, level, and discharge.

name: Ecohydrology
description: The study of interactions between water and ecosystems.

name: Urban Hydrology
description: The study of water movement and drainage in urban areas.

name: Physical Volcanology
description: The study of volcanic eruption processes and products.

name: Volcano Monitoring
description: The observation and forecasting of volcanic activity and hazards.

name: Magma Dynamics
description: The study of magma generation, ascent, and eruption.

name: Pedology
description: The study of soil formation, classification, and morphology.

name: Soil Chemistry
description: The chemical composition and reactions of soils.

name: Soil Physics
description: The physical properties of soils including water and heat flow.

name: Soil Biology
description: The study of organisms living in soil and their functions.

name: Edaphology
description: The study of soil in relation to plant growth and fertility.

name: Ice Sheet Dynamics
description: The study of the flow and behavior of ice sheets.

name: Geocryology
description: The study of permafrost and frozen ground.

name: Planetary Geomorphology
description: The study of landforms on other planetary bodies.

name: Impact Cratering
description: The study of craters and processes formed by meteorite impacts.

name: Ore Genesis
description: The study of how mineral deposits form.

name: Petroleum Geology
description: The geological study of petroleum occurrence and reservoirs.

name: Mining Geology
description: The geological work supporting mineral extraction.

name: Geomicrobiology
description: The study of microbial interactions with geological materials and processes.

name: Physical Limnology
description: The study of the physical processes of lakes, such as mixing and stratification.

name: Chemical Limnology
description: The chemistry of inland waters and their nutrient cycles.

name: Biological Limnology
description: The study of organisms and food webs in freshwater ecosystems.
